verses.zh: 大卫王对会众说：「我儿子所罗门是　神特选的，还年幼娇嫩；这工程甚大，因这殿不是为人，乃是为耶和华　神建造的。
verses.en: King David said to the entire assembly: “My son Solomon, the one whom God has chosen, is just an inexperienced young man,[NOTE:1] and the task is great, for this palace is not for man, but for the Lord God.
notes: Heb “a young man and tender.”
verses.commentary:
29:1 "the entire assembly" The groups of leaders are mentioned in 1 Chr. 23:2; 28:1. Here, it refers to
"all Israel" (cf. 1 Chr. 29:23,25,26), which is a common theme in Chronicles. The post-exilic period was
a reunification of the kingdoms of Judah and Israel.

▣ "whom alone God has chosen" See note at 1 Chr. 28:4-6.

Solomon's choice to be king is surprising.

- He was not the oldest male child.

- He was a son of Bathsheba, which reminded everyone of David's sin, weakness, and abuse of power.

This surely does show God's sovereignty in His choices! Another example of God's sovereignty is that as
wives of the Patriarchs were often barren; He had to specifically give them children (i.e., Sarah, Rachel).
Also how no other firstborn son of the Patriarchs succeeded his father as leader of the family.

- Isaac ‒ not Esau

- Jacob ‒ not Reuben

- Jesse ‒ not the oldest child

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

▣ "is still young and inexperienced" David gives this as the reason he did all the preparations for building
the temple (cf. 1 Chr. 22:5). The Bible does not give us Solomon's age when he became king. Jewish
tradition says he was between 12-14 years old.

▣

NASB
"temple"

NKJV footnote, NJB
"palace"

NRSV, JPSOA footnote
"fortress"

LXX, REB, Peshitta
- omitted -

This term (BDB 108, KB 123, cf. 1 Chr. 29:19) is not the usual term for "temple," but for "fortress"
or "citadel" (cf. 2 Chr. 17:12; 27:4; Esther; Neh. 2:8; 7:2; Dan. 8:2). Only here in the OT is it translated "temple."

verses.zh: 我为我　神的殿已经尽力，预备金子做金器，银子做银器，铜做铜器，铁做铁器，木做木器，还有红玛瑙可镶嵌的宝石，彩石和一切的宝石，并许多汉白玉。
verses.en: So I have made every effort[NOTE:1] to provide what is needed for the temple of my God, including the gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood,[NOTE:2] as well as a large amount of onyx, settings of antimony and other stones, all kinds of precious stones, and alabaster.
notes: Heb “and according to all my strength.”
Heb “the gold for the gold, and the silver for the silver, and the bronze for the bronze, the iron for the iron, and the wood for the wood.”
verses.commentary:
29:2 Many of the gems mentioned are uncertain.

- onyx stone ‒ BDB 995 I, possibly carnelian (NEB) or lapis lazuli (cf. Job 28:16; Ezek. 28:13).

It was one of the stones on the breastplate of Aaron (cf. Exod. 28:20) and on his shoulders (cf. Exod. 39:27).

- inlaid stones ‒ BDB 571 used of the stones of the breastplate of the High Priest, cf. Exod. 25:7; 35:9,27

- stones of antimony ‒ BDB 806, KB 918, possibly

- dark mortar to set and highlight a colored stone/gem, cf. Isa. 54:11

- a particular dark gem stone

- stones of various colors ‒ This phrase may refer to geometric patterns of mosaic floors or panels (not pictures); uncut
colored stones were often arranged into shapes in the ANE (see IVP, Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 419).

- all kinds of precious stones ‒ these are not specified but are apparently different from the stones in #2

- alabaster ‒ BDB 1010, KB 1483; this Egyptian loan word was possibly the "alabaster" of Song of Songs 5:15 or "marble,"
cf. Esther 1:6. In the NT perfumed oils were kept in stone containers made of this rock (cf. Matt. 26:7; Mark 18:3; Luke 7:37).

- calcium carbonate

- calcium sulphate (i.e., gypsum)

verses.zh: 且因我心中爱慕我　神的殿，就在预备建造圣殿的材料之外，又将我自己积蓄的金银献上，建造我　神的殿，
verses.en: Now, to show my commitment to the temple of my God, I donate my personal treasure of gold and silver to the temple of my God, in addition to all that I have already supplied for this holy temple.
verses.commentary:
29:3-5 Another list is found in 1 Chr. 22:3-5,14. This material came from

- things taken in war

- personal gifts (cf. 1 Chr. 29:6-7)

- foreign taxation

The amounts here are different from 1 Chr. 22:14, both of which are unusually high; whether literal or literary
hyperbole is uncertain. See Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 242-243 or Gleason Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible Difficulties,
pp. 222-223.

verses.zh: 就是俄斐金三千他连得、精链的银子七千他连得，以贴殿墙。
verses.en: This includes 3,000 talents[NOTE:1] of gold from Ophir and 7,000 talents of refined silver for overlaying the walls of the buildings,
notes: See the note on the word “talents” in 19:6. Using the “light” standard talent of 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg) as the standard for calculation, David had supplied 101 tons (91,800 kg) of gold and 235.5 tons (214,200 kg) of silver.
verses.commentary:
29:4 "talents" Some parts of Solomon's temple were overlaid (BDB 376, KB 372, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) with gold and silver, but which buildings or parts of building is not specified.
2 Chronicles 3:8-9 says the inside of the Holy of Holies was covered with gold.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANCIENT NEAR EASTERN WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES

verses.zh: 金子做金器，银子做银器，并藉匠人的手制造一切。今日有谁乐意将自己献给耶和华呢？」
verses.en: for gold and silver items, and for all the work of the craftsmen. Who else wants to contribute to the Lord today?”
verses.commentary:
29:5 There is a recurrent use of "hand" as an idiom for action.

- done, 1 Chr. 29:5 ‒ lit. "by the hand of"

- consecrate, 1 Chr. 29:5 ‒ lit. "to fill the hand" (idiom for priests, cf. Exod. 28:41; Lev. 8:33)

- in care of, 1 Chr. 29:8 ‒ lit. "under the hand of"

- pledged, 1 Chr. 29:24 ‒ lit. "put a hand under Solomon"

This imagery is used of God in 1 Chr. 29:12,14,16

- "in Your hand," 1 Chr. 29:12

- "from Your hand," 1 Chr. 29:14,16

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

▣ "the craftsmen" This word (BDB 360) can refer to

- metal workers

- wood workers

- stone workers

Also note 1 Chr. 22:15, where specific craftsmen are mentioned.

▣ "willing" This VERB (BDB 621, KB 671) occurs often in this chapter (cf. 1 Chr. 29:5,6,9 [twice],
14,17 [twice]), more than any other context in the OT; only here in 1 Chronicles, and only once in 2 Chronicles (cf. 2 Chr. 17:16).
It focuses on human choice and willingness to give to God. God's sovereignty is magnified in 1 Chr. 29:11-13, but 29:14-17
focuses on human free will.

In some ways this parallels the generosity related to

- the tabernacle ‒ Exod. 35:5,21,22,29

- the second temple ‒ Ezra 1:6; 2:68; 3:5

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION (CALVINISM) VS. HUMAN FREE WILL (ARMINIANISM)

verses.zh: 于是，众族长和以色列各支派的首领、千夫长、百夫长，并监管王工的官长，都乐意献上。
verses.en: The leaders of the families, the leaders of the Israelite tribes, the commanders of units of a thousand and a hundred, and the supervisors of the king’s work contributed willingly.

verses.zh: 他们为　神殿的使用献上金子五千他连得零一万达利克，银子一万他连得，铜一万八千他连得，铁十万他连得。
verses.en: They donated for the service of God’s temple 5,000 talents[NOTE:1] and 10,000 darics[NOTE:2] of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
notes: See the note on the word “talents” in 19:6. Using the “light” standard talent of 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg) as the standard for calculation, the people donated 168.3 tons (153,000 kg) of gold, 336.5 tons (306,000 kg) of silver, 605.7 tons (550,800 kg) of bronze, and 3,365 tons (3,060,000 kg) of iron.

On the “daric” as a unit of measure, see BDB 204 s.v. דַּרְכְּמוֹן. Some have regarded the daric as a minted coin, perhaps even referring to the Greek drachma, but this is less likely.sn The daric was a unit of weight perhaps equal to between 8 and 9 grams (just under one-third of an ounce), so 10,000 darics of gold would weigh between 80 and 90 kilograms (between 176 and 198 pounds).
verses.commentary:
29:7 "darics" This (BDB 204, KB 232) is a rare word (here and Ezra 2:69; 8:27; Neh. 7:70-72). It could mean

- a Persian gold coin from

- Cyrus' days

- Darius' days

- an Assyrian word for a fraction of a mina

- another term for "drachma"

There were no coins in David's days, so, if it does refer to a later coin, it is an anachronism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COINS IN USE IN
PALESTINE IN JESUS' DAY

verses.zh: 凡有宝石的都交给革顺人耶歇，送入耶和华殿的府库。
verses.en: All who possessed precious[NOTE:1] stones donated them to the treasury of the Lord’s temple, which was under the supervision of Jehiel the Gershonite.
notes: The word “precious” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
29:8 "Jehiel the Gershonite" This Levite is mentioned in 1 Chr. 23:8; 26:21 as son of Ladan, son of Gershon.
Ladan may be the same as "Libni of 1 Chr. 6:17. He was in charge of the treasury.

There are eleven people in the OT with this name, which means "God is living" (BDB 313).

verses.zh: 因这些人诚心乐意献给耶和华，百姓就欢喜，大卫王也大大欢喜。
verses.en: The people were delighted with their donations, for they contributed to the Lord with a willing attitude;[NOTE:1] King David was also very happy.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “with a complete heart.”
Heb “And also David the king rejoiced with great joy.”

verses.zh: 所以，大卫在会众面前称颂耶和华说：「耶和华―我们的父，以色列的　神是应当称颂，直到永永远远的！
verses.en: David praised the Lord before the entire assembly:[NOTE:1] “O Lord God of our father Israel, you deserve praise forevermore!
notes: Heb “assembly, and David said.” The words “and David said” are redundant according to contemporary English style and have not been included in the translation.
verses.commentary:
29:10 "David blessed the Lord" The VERB (BDB 138, KB 159)
is used several times in this chapter.

- David blesses YHWH, 1 Chr. 29:10 (twice)

- the assembly is called on to bless YHWH, 1 Chr. 29:20 (twice)

YHWH is worthy of blessing (see Contextual Insights, D.).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

▣ "O Lord God of Israel our father, forever" See several Special Topics.

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (THE NAME)

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

- SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，尊大、能力、荣耀、强胜、威严都是你的；凡天上地下的都是你的；国度也是你的，并且你为至高，为万有之首。
verses.en: O Lord, you are great, mighty, majestic, magnificent, glorious, and sovereign[NOTE:1] over all the sky and earth! You, Lord, have dominion and exalt yourself as the ruler[NOTE:2] of all.
notes: The words “and sovereign” are added in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.
Heb “head.”
verses.commentary:
29:11 This verse reminds me of several prayers.

- This verse may be the OT source to Matt. 6:13b ("For Yours is the Kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen"),
which was a later scribal addition to Jesus' prayer, probably as it began to be used in a liturgical manner.

- Paul's prayer or quoted hymn/liturgy of 1 Tim. 1:17

- Jude's closing prayer (i.e., Jude, vv. 24-25)

- The prayer of praise to the Lamb in Rev. 5:13 (also note Rev. 4:11; 5:12)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

▣ "glory" This (BDB 802) can also mean "beauty" (cf. Isa. 3:18). It refers to "YHWH's "glorious name"
in 1 Chr. 29:12 (cf. Isa. 63:14).

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, LXX
"the victory"

TEV, REB
"length of days"

NJB
"splendor"

Peshitta
"the beauty"

This NOUN (BDB 664 I, KB 716 I) has several major meanings.

- victory in battle

- strength in battle ‒ Ps. 18:1; Lam. 3:18

- glory, splendor ‒ 1 Sam. 15:29

- duration ‒ Job 23:7; Ps. 74:3; Pro. 21:28; Isa. 34:10; Jer. 15:18; Dan. 7:18; Amos 1:11

All of these usages could fit this list of God's kingly attributes.

▣ "head over all" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM.

verses.zh: 丰富尊荣都从你而来，你也治理万物。在你手里有大能大力，使人尊大强盛都出于你。
verses.en: You are the source of wealth and honor;[NOTE:1] you rule over all. You possess strength and might to magnify and give strength to all.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “wealth and honor [are] from before you.”
Heb “and in your hand [is] strength and might, and [it is] in your hand to magnify and to give strength to all.”
verses.commentary:
29:12 "honor" This is the use of kabod (BDB 458, KB 455) in referring to humans. It denotes a position,
civil/religious, of high standing in the community and/or wealth (cf. 1 Chr. 29:28; Gen. 31:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

verses.zh: 我们的　神啊，现在我们称谢你，赞美你荣耀之名！
verses.en: Now, our God, we give thanks to you and praise your majestic name!
verses.commentary:
29:13 "we thank You" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THANKSGIVING.

▣ "Your glorious Name" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT) and
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT).

verses.zh: 「我算甚么，我的民算甚么，竟能如此乐意奉献？因为万物都从你而来，我们把从你而得的献给你。
verses.en: “But who am I and who are my people that we should be in a position to contribute this much?[NOTE:1] Indeed, everything comes from you, and we have simply given back to you what is yours.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “that we should retain strength to contribute like this.”
Heb “and from you we have given to you.”
verses.commentary:
29:14 "all things come from You" This is the biblical worldview (cf 1 Chr. 29:12; Ps. 50:9-12; 1 Cor. 4:7; James 1:17).
He owns everything and we are stewards (1 Chr. 29:16, "all is Yours").

verses.zh: 我们在你面前是客旅，是寄居的，与我们列祖一样。我们在世的日子如影儿，不能长存（或译：没有长存的指望）。
verses.en: For we are resident foreigners and temporary settlers[NOTE:1] in your presence, as all our ancestors were;[NOTE:2] our days are like a shadow on the earth, without security.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew terms ger (גֵּר; “resident foreigner”) and toshav (תּוֹשָׁב; “resident/dweller”) have similar meanings. They are not used here with the technical distinctions of most references in Mosaic Law. 1 Chron 29:15 takes up this language from Lev 25:23 where the terms emphasize that Israel would be a guest on God’s land. This is a privileged but dependent position; they did not own the land. Cf. also Ps 39:12 and Gen 23:4.
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 18, 20).
Or perhaps “hope.”
verses.commentary:
29:15 Our earthly experience since the fall of Genesis 3 has been one of pain, suffering, unfairness, evil, and
exploitation. This is not the world God intended it to be (see John Wenham, The Goodness of God).

The Israelites saw themselves as sojourners (BDB 59) and tenants (BDB 444), which may come from
Lev. 25:23 or possibly Ps. 39:12; 119:19,54. Abraham (cf. Gen. 23:4) and Jacob (cf. Gen. 47:9) were sojourners and
strangers in a foreign land. The Bible views God's people as pilgrims (cf. 1 Chr. 16:19-20). We are on the way to His
eternal city (cf. Heb. 11:8-10; 12:22; 13:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL

▣ "our days on the earth are like a shadow" This imagery speaks of the temporary and transitory nature
of human existence (cf. Job 14:1-2; Ps. 90:5-6; 102:11; 103:15-16; Isa. 40:6-8; 1 Pet. 1:24-25).

▣ "there is no hope" This is true if there is no God (cf. 1 Thess. 4:13). Usually this term (BDB 876 I) has
God as the explicit object). It is not true for God's people (cf. Isa. 40:86; 55:6-12). He Himself is their hope.

It is possible (because it has no object here) that "no hope" refers to "no homeland," which is a
continuation of the imagery of Israel as "strangers and sojourners."

The Peshitta has "For we are like the proverb of vapor and of the potter, and we are sojourners before
You and a small people in the world, but You ruled over our fathers of old, and You commanded them the way they should
walk and live."

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神啊，我们预备这许多材料，要为你的圣名建造殿宇，都是从你而来，都是属你的。
verses.en: O Lord our God, all this wealth, which we have collected to build a temple for you to honor your holy name, comes from you; it all belongs to you.
verses.commentary:
29:16 "Your Holy Name" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE and
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT).

▣ "all is Yours" See note at 1 Chr. 29:11.

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，我知道你察验人心，喜悦正直；我以正直的心乐意献上这一切物。现在我喜欢见你的民在这里都乐意奉献与你。
verses.en: I know, my God, that you examine thoughts[NOTE:1] and are pleased with integrity. With pure motives[NOTE:2] I contribute all this; and now I look with joy as your people who have gathered here contribute to you.
notes: Heb “a heart.”
Heb “with integrity of heart.”
verses.commentary:
29:17 "You try the heart" God tests humans' motives (cf. Job 7:18; 23:10; Ps. 7:9; 11:5; 17:31; 26:2; 66:10;
139:1,23. God knows the motives and intents of the human heart. Reward and judgment are possible because God
knows the intent (cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; 16:7; 1 Kgs. 8:39; 1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 6:30; Job 13:9; Ps. 7:9; 33:15; 44:21; 139:1-4;
Pro. 15:11; 21:2; 24:12; Jer. 11:20; 17:9-10; 20:12; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27).

The Tyndale OT Commentary Series, vol. 10, p. 270, makes the point that the word "heart" appears
five times in 1 Chr. 29:17-19.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TESTS HIS PEOPLE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "uprightness. . .integrity" Both of these English words translate the Hebrew root BDB 449, which is
common in all ANE languages for God as a standard of ethical behavior. This same concept is expressed by
"righteousness". David was not "sinless" or even always ethical but he was in relationship with YHWH. David had a wholly
devoted heart (cf. Deut. 18:13; 1 Kgs. 8:61; 15:14; 2 Kgs. 28:3; 1 Chr. 20:9-10; 29:9,17-19; Isa. 38:3). This is theologically
related to the NT concept of justification by grace through faith (i.e., Abraham, Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3; Gal. 3:6; and Israel,
Exod. 4:5,31; 2 Chr. 20:20; Isa. 43:10).

Notice the word "reckoned" in Gen. 15:6 is used in 1 Chr. 29:18, translated by NASB as "intentions
of the heart." These verses (i.e., 1 Chr. 29:17-19) integrate YHWH's sovereign grace and His people's obedience to
His covenant. We need a perfect heart which leads to obedience (cf. 1 Chr. 28:8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH, AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OLD TESTAMENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, TRUST (NT)

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们列祖亚伯拉罕、以撒、以色列的　神啊，求你使你的民常存这样的心思意念，坚定他们的心归向你，
verses.en: O Lord God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, always maintain these motives of your people and keep them devoted to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “keep this permanently with respect to the motive of the thoughts of the heart of your people, and make firm their heart to you.”
verses.commentary:
29:18-19 David asks YHWH these prayer requests.

- preserve this forever ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE; the "this" could refer to

- the devotion of the Patriarchs (TEV, NET)

- God's purpose in calling the Patriarchs (NRSV, NJB, REB)

- God's promises to the Patriarchs (LXX, Peshitta, JPSOA)

- the Israelites remembering the Patriarchs

- direct their heart to You ‒ BDB 465, KB 464, Hiphil IMPERATIVE (possibly repeat of d. above)

- give Solomon a perfect heart to keep Your commandments ‒ BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERATIVE;
this was crucial, cf. 1 Chr. 28:8-9)

29:18 "the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. . ."This verse surely expresses the heart of the Chronicler for the
people of God of his day!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

verses.zh: 又求你赐我儿子所罗门诚实的心，遵守你的命令、法度、律例，成就这一切的事，用我所预备的建造殿宇。」
verses.en: Make my son Solomon willing to obey your commands, rules, and regulations, and to complete building the palace for which I have made preparations.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and to Solomon my son give a complete heart to keep your commands, your rules and your regulations, and to do everything, and to build the palace [for] which I have prepared.”

verses.zh: 大卫对全会众说：「你们应当称颂耶和华―你们的　神。」于是会众称颂耶和华―他们列祖的　神，低头拜耶和华与王。
verses.en: David told the entire assembly: “Praise the Lord your God!” So the entire assembly praised the Lord God of their ancestors; they bowed down and stretched out flat on the ground before the Lord and the king.
verses.commentary:
29:20 "all the assembly blessed the Lord" This involved inward devotion and trust
as well as outward acts.

- speaking liturgy, prayers, or songs ‒ Jer. 33:3; Joel 2:32; Acts 2:21; Rom. 10:9-13

- bowing ‒ Gen. 24:26,48; Exod. 4:31; 12:27; 34:8; Num. 22:31; 2 Chr. 20:18; 29:30; Neh. 8:6

Notice they "worshiped" YHWH but "honored" the king (cf. Gen. 43:28; 1 Sam. 24:8; 1 Kgs. 1:14,31).

They are the same word (BDB 1005, KB 295) but with different connotations.

verses.zh: 次日，他们向耶和华献平安祭和燔祭，就是献公牛一千只，公绵羊一千只，羊羔一千只，并同献的奠祭；又为以色列众人献许多的祭。那日，他们在耶和华面前吃喝，大大欢乐。
verses.en: The next day they made sacrifices and offered burnt sacrifices to the Lord (1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs), along with their accompanying drink offerings and many other sacrifices for all Israel.
verses.commentary:
29:21 "they made sacrifices" 1 Kings 8:62-63 records the sacrifices at the dedication of Solomon's temple.

▣ "all Israel" This is the recurrent theme of Chronicles (cf. 1 Chr. 29:21,23,25,26). It reflects the historical
reality and theological hope of the post-exilic period.

29:22a This describes a covenant meal which sealed the agreement or possibly better, "an ordination
offering" (BDB 1023, KB 1536; cf. Exod. 29:19-34; Lev. 7:37; 8:22-33). Part of the "peace offering" was given to
YHWH on the altar, part to the priests, and the rest was consumed by the community of faith.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

verses.zh: 他们奉耶和华的命再膏大卫的儿子所罗门作王，又膏撒督作祭司。
verses.en: They held a feast[NOTE:1] before the Lord that day and celebrated.[NOTE:2] Then they designated Solomon, David’s son, as king a second time;[NOTE:3] before the Lord they anointed him as ruler and Zadok as priest.
notes: Heb “they ate and drank.”
Heb “with great joy.”
See 1 Chr 23:1, where David had previously designated Solomon as king over Israel.

verses.zh: 于是所罗门坐在耶和华所赐的位上，接续他父亲大卫作王，万事亨通；以色列众人也都听从他。
verses.en: Solomon sat on the Lord’s throne as king in place of his father David; he was successful and all Israel was loyal to him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “listened to him.”
verses.commentary:
29:23 "the throne of the Lord" The throne of Israel belonged to YHWH
(cf. 1 Sam. 8:7; 1 Chr. 28:5).

Solomon and all Judean kings were His earthly representatives.

verses.zh: 众首领和勇士，并大卫王的众子，都顺服所罗门王。
verses.en: All the officers and warriors, as well as all of King David’s sons, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “placed a hand under Solomon the king.”
verses.commentary:
29:24 Notice the people who recognize and affirm Solomon's succession.

- the officials (civic, religious, military)

- the mighty men (David's private mercenaries, cf. 1 Kgs. 1:8,10,38,44)

- the other royal sons of David (royal princes)

▣ "pledged" This is literally, "put a hand under Solomon." Similar idioms of loyalty using "hand" are
found in Ezra 10:19; Lam. 5:6; Ezek. 17:18. See notes at 1 Chr. 29:5.

verses.zh: 耶和华使所罗门在以色列众人眼前甚为尊大，极其威严，胜过在他以前的以色列王。
verses.en: The Lord greatly magnified Solomon before all Israel and bestowed on him greater majesty than any king of Israel before him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and gave to him glory of kingship which there was not concerning every king before him over Israel.”
verses.commentary: 29:25 Keep in mind all the glory of Solomon is eclipsed by Jesus the ultimate son of David (cf. Luke 11:31)!

verses.zh: 耶西的儿子大卫作以色列众人的王，
verses.en: David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.

verses.zh: 作王共四十年：在希伯仑作王七年，在耶路撒冷作王三十三年。
verses.en: He reigned over Israel forty years; he reigned in Hebron seven years and in Jerusalem[NOTE:1] thirty-three years.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
29:27 The Chronicler does not mention that David reigned over Judah for only seven years and then over
all Israel for thirty three (cf. 2 Sam. 5:4,5; 1 Kgs. 2:11; 1 Chr. 3:4). Here again the focus is on "all Israel."

verses.zh: 他年纪老迈，日子满足，享受丰富、尊荣，就死了。他儿子所罗门接续他作王。
verses.en: He died at a good old age, having enjoyed long life, wealth, and honor.[NOTE:1] His son Solomon succeeded him.
notes: Heb “satisfied with days, wealth, and honor.”
verses.commentary:
29:28 David's death was not viewed as a tragedy, but a quiet close to a blessed life of service and devotion to God.

- long reign over united Israel

- long life (idiom implying "grey" hair, cf. Gen. 15:15 Jdgs. 8:32)

- full of days (cf. Gen. 25:8; 35:29; 1 Chr. 23:1; Job 42:17)

- prosperous life

- honorable life

- a son succeeded him

- he affected Israel and the surrounding nations (1 Chr. 29:30)

verses.zh: 大卫王始终的事都写在先见撒母耳的书上和先知拿单并先见迦得的书上。
verses.en: King David’s accomplishments, from start to finish, are recorded in the Annals of Samuel the prophet, the Annals of Nathan the prophet, and the Annals of Gad the prophet.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the events of David the king, the former and the latter, look they are written in the annals of Samuel the seer, and in the annals of Nathan the prophet, and in the annals of Gad the seer.”

verses.zh: 他的国事和他的勇力，以及他和以色列并列国所经过的事都写在这书上。
verses.en: Recorded there are all the facts about his reign and accomplishments, and an account of the events that involved him, Israel, and all the neighboring kingdoms.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “with all his reign and his might, and the times which passed over him and over Israel and over all the kingdoms of the lands.”
verses.commentary:
29:30 "and on all the kingdoms of the lands" This phrase occurs only in Chronicles (cf. 2 Chr. 12:8; 17:10; 20:29)
and refers to the surrounding nations. YHWH's actions have always had "the nations" on His heart.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How is this chapter related to 1 Chr. 23:2 and 28:1?

- Why does 1 Chr. 28:4-6 emphasize YHWH's choice of Solomon?

- Why is the weight of precious metals different between 1 Chr. 29:7 and 22:14?

- How is 1 Chr. 29:11 linked to Jesus' model prayer of Matthew 6?

- Explain your understanding of the literary purpose of 1 Chr. 29:5.

- Does 1 Chr. 29:17-19 relate to 28:8-9?

- Is the covenant with Solomon conditional or unconditional?

- How is 1 Chr. 29:21 related to 1 Kgs. 8:62-63?

- What does "a second time" mean in 1 Chr. 29:22b?

- Does 1 Chr. 29:29 refer to lost books or the books of Samuel and Kings?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter records David's prayer to YHWH at the time of the succession of Solomon.

- There are several terms used to refer to Israel's Deity.

- Elohim, 1 Chr. 29:1,16,18

- Eloah, 1 Chr. 29:2,3 (twice), 10,13,17,20 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)

- YHWH, 1 Chr. 29:5,8,9,10,11 (twice), 20 (thrice), 21,22,23,25 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)

- Father, 1 Chr. 29:10 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD)

- There are several repeated theological themes.

- YHWH chose Solomon, 1 Chr. 20:1; 1 Chr. 28:4-6

- Solomon must keep the covenant commandments (i.e., conditional covenant, cf. 1 Chr. 29:19; 22:12-13; 28:7-8; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT and
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- David's assembling materials for the new temple, 1 Chr. 29:2-5; 22:3-5,14-16

- the focus on proper whole-hearted commitment to YHWH, 1 Chr. 29:17,19; 28:9; Deut. 18:13; 1 Kgs. 8:61; 15:14;
2 Kgs. 20:3; Isa. 38:3; attitude in worship and spiritual matters is preeminent (cf. Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26;
Ezek. 44:9); God looks at the heart before the hand!

- Notice the description of God in David's prayer (1 Chr. 29:10-19).

- He is Israel's Father forever, 1 Chr. 20:10

- He has

- the greatness (BDB 153)

- the power (BDB 150)

- the glory (BDB 802)

- the victory (BDB 664 I)

- the majesty (BDB 217 I)

- all in heaven and on earth (1 Chr. 29:11,16)

- dominion (lit. kingdom), 1 Chr. 29:11

- He is head over all, 1 Chr. 29:11

- riches and honor come from Him, 1 Chr. 29:12

- He rules over all

- power (BDB 470)

- might (BDB 150)

- He can

- make great (BDB 152, INFINITIVE)

- give strength (BDB 304, INFINITIVE), 1 Chr. 29:12

- He tests the heart (BDB 103, PARTICIPLE), 1 Chr. 29:17

- He delights in

- uprightness (BDB 449)

- integrity of heart (BDB 449), 1 Chr. 29:17

- He is actively involved in people's motives

- gives a perfect heart

- keeps the human heart perfect, 1 Chr. 29:18-19

Wow! What a God!
